messages:
anya: quick data drop — halcyon9b quant sweep finished (int8 vs int6). ran longform QA, summarization, and hallucination checks. short summary below, full notebook link: https://redwood/gist/halcyon-sweep

zara: tl;dr numbers: int8 baseline, int6 smaller model artifacts. quality delta is small overall but a few slices show regressions. table:```
metric      | int8  | int6  | delta (int6 - int8)
-----------|-------|-------|-------------------
EM (QA)    | 74.8  | 72.1  | -2.7
ROUGE-L    | 38.5  | 37.9  | -0.6
Halluc rate| 3.6%  | 6.0%  | +2.4pp
Latency p50 | 120ms | 95ms  | -25ms
Token cost  | $0.0024/token | $0.0015/token | -37%
```

jules: infra notes: int6 fits 2x A100 80GB with batch=8 at target latency; int8 needs 3rd card for peak throughput. int6 reduces mem pressure and allows 1.8x throughput for cost-sensitive fleet.

mike: product question — which slices show hallucination bump? is it long-context multi-doc QA or factual retrieval?

zara: mostly multi-doc QA and citation-sensitive prompts (examples in gist). short prompts unaffected. regression correlates with self-consistency decoding on int6.

ev al-bot: [auto] eval-run 1769998895 completed. regression alerts: hallucination +2.4pp (p<0.01) on slice: multi-doc-cite.

sam: from GTM lens — we need crisp guidance. customers will care about accuracy-first defaults. offering a cheaper opt-in tier ok, but we must avoid product regressions hurting trust.

anya: recommendation proposal:
- default route = int8 for product-facing QA and citation features (preserve quality).
- offer int6 as "economy" routing for non-citation flows (summarization, short chat) with explicit label and lower price.
- add slice-based routing: detect multi-doc/citation prompts and force int8.
- rollout plan: 2-week canary on 10% of low-risk traffic, run continuous slice evals and RPS/latency monitoring.

jules: ops checklist: config flags for routing by slice, metrics for halluc rate, enable progressive rollout via console with canary weight. need infra ticket for extra int8 capacity buffer.

mike: pricing ask: what cost delta should we show to customers? seems ~35-40% token savings for int6. can we present per-100k-token math?

anya: simple example: 100k tokens -> int8 = $240, int6 = $150, save $90 -> 37.5% cheaper. call it ~35% to be conservative.

sam: ok — GTM copy: "Halcyon 9B — Economy (int6): ~35% lower cost. Best for summaries and chat. Accuracy-critical features default to Standard (int8)." will draft.

zara: operationally add gating: if hallucination delta > +1.0pp in canary, auto-roll back.

ev al-bot: [auto] monitor created: halcyon9b-quant-canary-monitor. triggers: halluc_delta>1.0pp OR EM_delta<-1.5. alert -> #eng-ml incident if fired.

anya: final call: recommend product default = int8, opt-in economy = int6 with slice routing and auto-rollback rules. action items:
- jules: infra buffer ticket (#3421) + routing flags (ETA 3d)
- zara: add canary eval slice and dashboards (ETA 2d)
- sam/mike: GTM copy + pricing (ETA EOD Fri)
- anya: roll Canary config and run 2-week canary (start Mon)

mike: sounds good. thanks all. :thumbsup:

jules: noted. creating infra ticket now. :gear:
